chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfaly, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said regarding a man to whom it was said, 'You did such and such', and he said, 'No, by Allah, I did not do it', although he had indeed done it. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'A lie is what he has lied; he should seek forgiveness from Allah for it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a false oath taken in denial of an act?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) quoting Imam Ali (AS), clarifies the ruling on a false oath taken in denial of an act one has actually committed. It emphasizes that even if the denial is technically true in a specific context or meant to avoid a specific liability, if it involves a false claim of non-action when action occurred, it constitutes a lie requiring seeking forgiveness (istighfar). The narration highlights the importance of sincerity in oaths and the spiritual consequence of lying under oath, even if the core fact is disputed.
